name: Well pump and pressure tank

comps.spec: Submersible pump: Franklin's FPS 4-inch complete pumps run 1/2–1.5 hp on 230 V, with 115 V only at 1/2 hp; the 1.5 hp one tops out at 187 m (615 ft) of head with the flow shut off (Franklin FPS). Pulling it needs two people and a plan so the pipe isn't dropped
comps.loc: Down the well on the drop pipe

comps.spec: Above-ground jet pump, 1/2–1 hp. A shallow-well jet draws from about 6 m (20 ft) down at most, a deep-well one about 30 m (100 ft) (Wisconsin DNR DG-022). A.Y. McDonald: 7.6 m (25 ft) total suction lift, pipe losses included, at sea level, 0.3 m less per 300 m of altitude (A.Y. McDonald jet pumps).
Pressure tank with a rubber bladder, 20–120 litres
Pressure switch, about 30/50 or 40/60 psi, with heavy contacts
comps.loc: On the pipe by the tank

comps.spec: Submersible drop cable, 10–12 AWG copper, as long as the well is deep

comps.loc: Grey control box on the wall

comps.spec: Check valves, foot valve and pressure relief valve
Poly or PVC drop pipe, 25–32 mm

boards.loc: Constant-pressure controller on the wall (some newer systems)

notes: The well itself is the real prize. A submersible needs a large generator or inverter to start; once pump and pipe are out, a narrow bucket on a rope still lifts water.

sources.title: Wisconsin DNR DG-022: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, Driven Point (Sand Point) Wells (PUB-DG-022, 2024)
A.Y. McDonald jet pumps: A.Y. McDonald Mfg. Co., Jet Pumps Installation Instructions (8100 and 8500 shallow-well series)
Franklin FPS: Franklin Electric, FPS TRI-SEAL 4-inch submersible well pumps, residential duty (product page and model list)
